subject.title: [Bug]:  Session status blind spot | Sessions in done state excluded from context saturation monitoring — agents run dead for hours undetected

question: Should terminal `done` sessions with saturated context become native diagnostics or health alerts, and what threshold and action surface should own that behavior?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested fix changes monitoring semantics and could create noisy alerts or unsafe recovery unless maintainers choose the policy first.

options.title: Add a narrow diagnostic alert
options.body: Surface saturated terminal sessions as observe-only diagnostics or health warnings using existing context-budget data, then defer automatic recovery until live proof supports it.

options.title: Add alert plus recovery
options.body: Warn and automatically reset, compact, or release affected sessions, accepting higher behavior and upgrade risk for faster fleet recovery.

options.title: Keep this external for now
options.body: Leave terminal context-saturation monitoring to operator scripts or plugins until a broader session-health contract is designed.

recommendation.title: Add a narrow diagnostic alert
recommendation.body: Surface saturated terminal sessions as observe-only diagnostics or health warnings using existing context-budget data, then defer automatic recovery until live proof supports it.

likelyOwner.reason: The current checkout routes both the diagnostic heartbeat and session-row projection through areas recently attributed to this person, making them the best available policy-routing owner from the history checked.
